issues.title: OpenCode pane cannot scroll up or down
issues.symptom: In an OpenCode pane the terminal is on the alternate screen, where TermFleet's grid has no scrollback. Home/End/PageUp/PageDown were intercepted unconditionally and applied to that empty history, so the keys were swallowed and the TUI never received them - nothing could scroll. Wheel input is unaffected.
issues.guard: tests/terminal-viewport.spec.ts -g "alternate-screen navigation keys"

evidence.note: Second root cause found: terminalWheelAction only forwarded the wheel when mouseReport && altScreen, so an OpenCode pane (mouse claimed, primary screen) had the wheel routed to TermFleet's empty history. Now: mouseReport && (altScreen || hasHistory === false) -> mouse-report. Note the honest uncertainty: the earlier 'no mouse mode' scan read a TRUNCATED scrollback file, so it could not rule out a startup-time mouse enable; the authoritative mode lives in the grid.

Live geometry shows the scroll path working where history exists: panes ce928f5a and d13d04fa recorded hasHistory=true with displayOffset 5 and e65833e8 with displayOffset 1, i.e. the grid viewport really scrolled. All observed terminals are MAP nodes (never split), and no navigation-key decisions were recorded in the sampling window, so the swallowed-key invariant is wired but not yet exercised in live use.

issues.title: Terminal draws half-finished repaints and looks jumbled
issues.symptom: OpenCode panes intermittently render jumbled text: stray characters at the edge, fragments of one line mixed into another, and half-drawn screens. OpenCode wraps every full repaint in a synchronized-output block (?2026h ... ?2026l) precisely so the terminal shows it atomically, but TermFleet only stripped the markers so they would not print as text and never honoured the block: every feed marked the grid dirty and the 60Hz emitter published whatever the screen looked like mid-repaint.
issues.guard: cargo test --lib vt_grid:: (synchronized_output_markers_open_and_release_the_publish_hold, a_held_repaint_publishes_atomically_and_never_stalls)

evidence.note: Live stream from pane terminal-7259675f-3450-4ec0-a886-c96609705f1d (cwd bots+automation): 1,200 ?2026h/?2026l pairs, 7,081 absolute cursor-positioning calls, zero line feeds. vt_grid.rs strip_unsupported_control_sequences consumed the markers so they never render as text, but feed() unconditionally set dirty and bumped revision, and the 60Hz emitter published on the next tick, so a repaint spanning more than one tick reached the canvas as a mix of the old and new screen. TermState now records sync_output_since and the emitter holds publication through the block, with a 120ms fail-safe so a missed ?2026l can never stall a pane.

cargo test --lib: 204 passed, 0 failed. The two new vt_grid tests pass; dropping the ?2026h hold (sync_output_since never set) fails synchronized_output_markers_open_and_release_the_publish_hold with '?2026h must open the publish hold' at vt_grid.rs:2126, while the pure should_publish_frame test correctly still passes (the wiring was mutated, not the decision). Fail-safe covered: a block open past SYNC_OUTPUT_MAX_HOLD (120ms) publishes anyway.

evidence.note: paste-debug.log 2026-09-30 19:49-19:52: 12 bursts of 4-15 clipboard writes, each within ~1 s of a sidebar-focus map jump; a Ctrl+V at 19:51:59 read len=0.
